text:
anya: Quick callout 1: I mocked a denser compare table that hides long descriptions and adds a compact filter row. Putting this here for feedback.

samir: Looks promising. Two things: overflow for filter pills on small screens, and where do perf badges live? Inline or a right-hand column?

lina: Accessibility first: visible focus rings on pills, aria-expanded for row details, and screenreader labels for badges. Use shapes + text, not color alone.

mike: From infra: cached perf numbers are fine inline. For full benchmark context we should lazy-load on hover/focus to avoid extra calls.

jas: UX: inline badges are faster for glance comparisons but clutter at narrow widths. Right column is cleaner and we can add a toggle in catalog settings to persist preference.

anya: Good idea on toggle. Also thinking about pin flow: inline toggle in row vs modal. My vote is inline toggle with optional "Add note" modal for enterprise audit.

samir: Agree. Inline for speed, modal only when user clicks 'Add note' or when tenant policy requires a note. Toast confirmation should read: "Pinned model v2.1 to /chat 1: undo".

lina: I'll write a short a11y checklist for the PR: focus styles, aria-pressed for pin, aria-live for lazy content, contrast >=4.5 for small badge text.

anya: Thanks. I'll update the mocks with right-column badges + compact filter row and attach the a11y checklist. :thumbsup:
